findings.source: VaultCommon.sol _findTokenIndex: revert TokenNotRegistered(token); Vault.sol:emit Swap(pool, tokenIn, tokenOut, amountIn, amountOut, swapFeePercentage, totalSwapFees)
findings.issue: Custom errors and event data built at the free-memory pointer are printed as raw memory with lengths like '_474 - mem[64] + 36', although the text just bound _474 = mem[64]: the store mem[mem[64]] = selector might alias the pointer word itself, so the pointer is re-read. The 158 reverts and 7 events lose their arguments (the P2 regex counts only call arguments).
findings.rule: Same as the P2 root cause in c00578: track mem[64] >= 0x80 (every store to it is a constant >= 0x80 or a non-wrapping increment), so mem[mem[64] + k] (k >= 0) never aliases mem[64..95]; then _474 - mem[64] folds to 0 and the revert reads 'revert with TokenNotRegistered(address(_460))'.

findings.issue: When the mapping key is a 20-byte slice of a memory word (the pool address inside the copied params struct), the slot is printed as a raw hash and the access as stor[_N]; when the slot is recognised, the key is a concat of memory slices instead of address(mem[160]) or the index value just stored in mem[0].
findings.rule: Bytes(12, 0) ++ mem[a + 12 len 20] is address(mem[a]) for word-aligned a, so sha3(Bytes(12, 0), mem[a + 12 len 20], k) is the slot of storK[address(mem[a])]; a key read from mem[0] right after 'mem[0] = v' is v (fold the keccak scratch store into the key).

findings.source: Vault.sol:1309-1313 bufferBalances = PackedTokenBalance.toPackedBalance(bufferBalances.getBalanceRaw() + amountInUnderlying - vaultUnderlyingDeltaHint, bufferBalances.getBalanceDerived() + vaultWrappedDeltaHint - amountOutWrapped);
findings.issue: The packed (raw, derived) pair is written as whole-word arithmetic on the old word (P15), and its overflow check multiplies by -2^128 printed as a 39-digit decimal while the same term elsewhere on the line is '(_18 << 128)'.
findings.rule: Print c * x with c = -2^k as -(x << k) (and 2^k * x as x << k); after the BalanceOverflow checks prove each half < 2^128, print the packed store as (derived' << 128) + raw' with raw' and derived' named.

findings.issue: The immutables read as 0 (solc leaves zeros before deployment): the fallback delegates to address 0, the unlocked flag, the non-zero-delta counter and the session id are all transient[0] and the token deltas are transient[sha3(token, 0)], so unlock() always ends in BalanceNotSettled after setting the flag, and WrapAmountTooSmall checks fold away. The text is faithful to this bytecode.

notes: Reviewed: the 8 small functions in full (transfer, transferFrom with the try/catch emitApproval whose failure is ignored, sendTo with SafeERC20 checked against OZ _safeTransfer, settle, unlock with Address.functionCall, getPoolTokenCountAndIndexOfToken, reentrancyGuardEntered, getVaultExtension) and the fallback/receive; erc4626BufferWrapOrUnwrap's wrap EXACT_OUT path in detail (asset check, previewMint/forceApprove/mint, query context via tx.origin, BalanceOverflow and packed balance write, _settleWrap reserve checks, _takeDebt/_supplyCredit); swap (995 lines), addLiquidity (2,080 lines) and removeLiquidity (2,165 lines) by structure (loops, hook calls, storage writes, events, reentrancy-guard sections: the second guard section comes from _loadPoolDataUpdatingBalancesAndYieldFees being nonReentrant). No semantic error found; the decrement of the delta counter without an underflow check is exact (the dominating 'if not transient[0]: revert' proves transient[0] >= 1, the slots being the same immutable 0). Loops: the pack lists 11 source loops, but the reached library code (not in the pack) adds 8: ScalingHelpers.copyToScaled18ApplyRateRoundDown/UpArray, InputHelpers.getSingleInputIndex, BasePoolMath.computeProportionalAmountsIn/Out, computeAddLiquidityUnbalanced (2 loops), computeRemoveLiquiditySingleTokenExactOut; all 19 are whiles (e.g. 2724 and 2808 are computeAddLiquidityUnbalanced's two loops, 2548/3271/4611... getSingleInputIndex). Of the 103 text whiles, 53 are plain memory-to-memory copies (ABI encodings for hook calls, events, decodes; P7), 4 storage-to-memory copies of _poolTokens and 3 struct-array allocations are rotated (P3, first element peeled, 'while idx - 1'), and swap's two _findTokenIndex loops are rotated with the empty case guarded before the loop (exact). Other things: 104 dead keccak-scratch stores ('mem[32] = 5 / mem[32] = 0 / mem[32] = 4 / mem[32] = 3' in a row, P8); the PoolData struct lives in memory and its fields are read as mem[mem[X + 416]] etc. (P14/P18); getSingleInputIndex/forceApprove print the mint call in both arms (P12); 'ext_call.success and ...' after the success branch is known (P11).
summary: Faithful on every path checked; readability is poor in the three big functions, where PoolData and the swap/liquidity params live in memory (fields as nested mem[] reads), 53 memory copies stay loops, custom errors and events built at the free-memory pointer print as raw memory, and mappings keyed by an address read from memory print as stor[sha3(...)]; immutables read as 0 (delegate 0x0, all transient guard slots at 0).
